summary:
SOL-7 is a browser-native, interactive 3D space exploration simulator and decision-driven educational story game designed to help children aged 7-12 explore space and become enthusiastic and curios about space.

During the mission, player can communicate with crew for decision making in deep space with four decisions which impact their next decision. These include four important astronaut training topics: radiation, life support, fuel management, and communication making learning knowledgeable and encouraging them to become curios about space. NASA's DONKI API provides real space-weather information, including solar flares, which is used in the radiation challenge.

Players register a personalized Astronaut Commander Dossier, walk across Earth Launch Complex 39A, launch aboard the SOL-7 Rocket to the 100 km Karman Line, navigate an interactive 8-planet + Moon 3D Solar System, execute a retro-propulsive landing on the Moon or Mars, and lead a 4-astronaut crew through 4 branching chapters grounded in real NASA Open Data (DONKI, DSN, OSDR, and ECLSS). Players can snap live 3D photos with the in-game EVA.
Camera and review them alongside their 4-Chapter Decision Flowchart Certificate.

What it does
SOL 7 Junior Astronaut Trainer is a browser game where players trains as an astronaut

to complete a story driven mission with experience of crew members. The game gives you as real as possible experience with a Pre-Flight Astronaut Registration & Live Dossier. Also 8-Planet + Moon 3D Solar System with landing on command Artemis Base Alpha (Moon) or Olympus Station (Mars). 4-Crew Branching Story Engine. In-Game EVA Camera, Photo Gallery & Final Progress Certificate.

Benefits and impact
The game lets kids aged 7-12 (and adults) learn by doing. It shows why real missions depend on managing radiation, oxygen, fuel, and communication. The game drives you in an actual deep space decision making. Transform passive space textbooks into an interactive leadership simulation.

NASA data
Connect live NASA DONKI API webhooks for real-time solar weather alerts.

• NASA DONKI (Solar Storms) & ECLSS (Water/O2 Recycling).

• NASA OSDR (Radiation Dosimetry) & DSN (14-min Signal Latency).

• Live WebGL EVA Camera stamps Mission Progress % onto every

Tools
Core Frontend & 3D Graphics:

• React 19 + TypeScript 5.8 for modular, type-safe state management.

• Three.js + @react-three/fiber + @react-three/drei for declarative 3D scenes.

• HTML5 2D Canvas API for procedural planetary textures & photo watermarks.

UI styling, Audio & Build Tooling:

• Tailwind CSS v4 + Lucide React Icons + Orbitron/Rajdhani typography.

• Native Browser Web Audio API for procedural sound synthesis.

• Vite 6 for fast bundling and optimized production builds.

ALL WITH USE OF GOOGLE'S ANTIGRAVITY AND GEMINI STUDIO.

Creativity
Instead of passive videos or articles, players live the mission from launch pad to lunar surface, with realistic visuals.

Interactive Solar System:

• Sun with pulsing corona + Mercury, Venus, Earth (Moon), Mars, Asteroid Belt (120 instanced rocks) Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune.

• Click any body to smoothly zoom and inspect NASA planetary.

Specials:

• Zero-install browser architecture makes 3D space labs accessible on any school laptop.

• Difficulty tiers (Cadet, Astronaut, Commander) + Science Glossary (G) adapt to ages 8–18+.

• Downloadable EVA photos give students a personalized artifact of their mission.
